title: BoThesis document upload and processing storage

decisions.raw_binary_fallback: PostgreSQL document_blobs, bounded to 20 MiB by default
decisions.provider_cache: documents.metadata keyed by provider and source fingerprint
decisions.deletion_policy: soft delete only; the application never physically removes retained content

documents.purpose: Canonical metadata, ownership, lineage, upload, lifecycle, and index readiness
constraints: exactly one of owner_user_id or tenant_id is set
upload idempotency is unique per personal owner
content_sha256 is null or lowercase SHA-256

document_blobs.purpose: Bounded fallback for raw bytes when object storage cannot be used

document_chunks.purpose: Canonical parsed chunks and source-location lineage
document_chunks.lifecycle: deleted_at tombstone; replacement reuses stable document and chunk keys

message_documents.purpose: Only durable association between messages and uploaded documents

authorization_links.lifecycle: revocation sets inactive/deleted_at and immediately excludes the rows from authorization

access_patterns: start or resume one upload by owner and idempotency key
validate one owner-visible document before direct model input
load or replace canonical chunks for on-demand indexing
link ordered documents to a user message and cited documents to an assistant message
replace deterministic vector points with active tenant, owner ACL, and chunk lineage
hide then idempotently tombstone PostgreSQL children, provider-cache entries, and vector points while retaining raw content

lifecycle.delete: active -> hidden -> deleted, with deleted_at tombstones on dependent records
lifecycle.retention: indefinite application retention; no hard-delete or purge operation
lifecycle.backup_boundary: PostgreSQL and object-store backup/versioning are deployment responsibilities
